title: Home-grill jingisukan
steps: Simmer the soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar for 2 minutes, cool, and stir in the garlic, ginger and apple.
Heat a griddle, a cast-iron pan or a table-top grill and oil it lightly.
Place the onion and pumpkin around the edges first, as they need longer.
Grill the lamb slices for 1 to 2 minutes per side until browned, adding the cabbage, pepper and sprouts as space allows.
Eat straight from the pan, dipping the lamb and vegetables in the sauce.
notes: Use sliced lamb from a butcher or buy frozen sliced lamb. Mutton is the traditional choice.

title: Cabbage monjayaki
steps: Whisk the flour, dashi, Worcestershire sauce and soy sauce into a thin, smooth batter.
Heat a griddle or large non-stick pan on medium-high and oil it. Fry the pork for 2 minutes.
Add the cabbage and spring onion, and stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes until slightly softened.
Push the mixture into a ring with a hole in the middle. Stir the batter and pour a little in the middle.
When it bubbles, draw the cabbage into the batter and mix everything. Spread thin and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, so that the bottom crisps.
Sprinkle with aonori and scrape up with small spatulas to eat.
notes: It is meant to be loose and sticky. Serve from the hot plate if you can.

title: Osaka-style okonomiyaki
steps: Stir the ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, soy sauce and sugar for the sauce.
Whisk flour, dashi and eggs into a smooth batter. Stir in the cabbage and spring onion until coated; the mix should be thick.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Pour in half the mixture and shape into a round about 2 cm thick.
Lay half the pork on top. Cook for 5 minutes until golden underneath, flip carefully and cook for 5 to 6 minutes more until cooked through.
Flip again so that the pork side is up, brush with sauce, zigzag with mayonnaise, and top with aonori and bonito flakes. Repeat for the second pancake.
notes: Do not press the pancake down while cooking, which makes it dense.

title: Takoyaki
steps: Whisk the flour, dashi and eggs into a very thin batter, with a pinch of salt. Rest for 15 minutes. Mix the sauce ingredients.
Heat a takoyaki pan and oil all the moulds generously.
Pour batter in until it overflows the moulds. Drop a piece of octopus in each, with a little spring onion and ginger.
When the edges set, about 2 minutes, cut the batter between moulds with a pick and push it back in. Add a little batter on top.
Rotate each ball a quarter turn with picks as they set, repeating until they are round and golden, about 8 to 10 minutes.
Serve with sauce, mayonnaise, aonori and bonito flakes.
notes: A takoyaki pan is needed; a Danish aebleskiver pan is a good alternative. The batter is much thinner than a pancake batter.

title: Home tonkotsu ramen
steps: Blanch the bones in boiling water for 10 minutes, drain and rinse them thoroughly to clean the scum off.
Return the bones to a clean pot with 3 l fresh water, onion, garlic and ginger. Boil hard, topping up with hot water to keep the bones covered, for 4 to 5 hours until the broth is cloudy and creamy.
Meanwhile, brown the pork belly in a pan, add 100 ml soy sauce, mirin, sugar and 300 ml water. Simmer covered for 1.5 hours, turning, then leave it in the liquid to cool. Slice thickly.
Strain the broth. Mix the tare ingredients, and put 1 tbsp in each of four bowls.
Cook the noodles for 1 to 2 minutes, drain well, and put in the bowls. Pour over 350 ml boiling hot broth per bowl.
Top with slices of chashu, egg, spring onion and nori.
notes: The cloudy broth needs a hard, rolling boil. Reduce the time to about 3 hours for a lighter, quicker home broth. Make the broth the day before and chill, then remove the excess fat if you like.

title: Goya champuru

ingredients.note: about 250 g, halved, seeds removed, thinly sliced

steps: Salt the bitter melon slices lightly, leave for 10 minutes, then squeeze out the liquid. This reduces bitterness.
Heat the oil in a wok or large pan. Crumble in the tofu and cook until golden on a few sides, about 3 minutes. Remove.
Fry the pork for 2 minutes, add the bitter melon and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, so that it stays crisp.
Return the tofu, add the sake, soy sauce and pepper, and toss.
Pour the eggs over, stirring until just set. Add half the bonito flakes, mix, and top with the rest. Serve with rice.
notes: Scrape out the white pith from the melon thoroughly. Luncheon meat is an authentic substitute for the pork.

title: Tofu and wakame miso soup
steps: Put the water and kombu in a pot and heat slowly. Remove the kombu just before it boils.
Add the bonito flakes, turn off the heat after 30 seconds and let them sink. Strain.
Return the dashi to a gentle simmer and add the tofu and wakame for 2 minutes.
Dissolve the miso through a small sieve into the soup. Do not boil it again, which spoils the aroma.
Add the spring onion and serve straight away.
notes: Use more miso for a stronger soup. For a vegetarian version replace the bonito with soaked dried shiitake in the dashi.

title: Kanto-style ozoni
steps: Make dashi by warming the kombu in the water, removing it before the boil, then steeping the bonito for a minute and straining.
Simmer the chicken, carrot and daikon in the dashi for 8 to 10 minutes, skimming off any scum.
Season the soup with soy sauce, salt and mirin.
Toast the mochi in a toaster oven or grill until puffed and golden, 4 to 5 minutes, or boil in a separate pot for a softer texture.
Place two mochi in each bowl, add the komatsuna, ladle on the soup and serve hot.
notes: Mochi is very sticky and a choking risk, especially for the elderly and young children. Cut it into small pieces and eat slowly.

title: Simmered black soybeans
steps: Combine the water, sugar, soy sauce and salt, and heat until the sugar dissolves. Add the beans and soak for 8 hours or overnight.
Bring to a boil in the soaking liquid, skim off any foam, then lower to a gentle simmer.
Keep at a bare simmer with a lid slightly ajar for about 4 hours, adding water as needed so the beans stay covered, until tender and soft enough to squash.
Turn off the heat and let the beans cool in the liquid, so they take on the syrup and keep a shiny, wrinkle-free skin.
Keep in the liquid in the fridge for up to a week; serve a few spoonfuls as part of New Year dishes.
notes: A pressure cooker cuts the time to about 1 hour. A rusty iron nail is sometimes added in traditional recipes to keep the black colour; it is not needed here.

title: Toshikoshi soba
steps: Warm the water with kombu, remove the kombu before boiling, add the bonito flakes, and strain after a minute to make dashi.
Add the soy sauce and mirin to the dashi and keep warm.
Boil the soba in plenty of water following the pack time, usually 4 to 6 minutes. Rinse under cold running water and drain well.
Briefly dip the noodles in hot water to warm them, and divide into two bowls.
Pour the hot broth over, scatter the spring onion on top and eat immediately.
notes: Add a piece of fried tofu or tempura if you like. 100% buckwheat soba is gluten-free but the soy sauce still contains wheat.
